title: Strong Gelfand pairs of the symplectic group Sp_4(q) where q is even: the maximal subgroup Sp_2(q^2):2 is not a strong Gelfand subgroup (Theorem 5.1)
author: Stephen P. Humphries, Joseph E. Marrow
work: Strong Gelfand pairs of the symplectic group, q even
difficulty_reason: The counted proof is the article's own total-character argument for the maximal subgroup Sp_2(q^2):2 of Sp_4(q), and it is not a qualification exercise. Even with the preliminary total-character lemmas, the character table of Sp_4(q) and the largest irreducible degree supplied as context, the author still has to determine, inside the proof, which irreducible characters of H = Sp_2(q^2) split and which fuse in G = Sp_2(q^2):2 (the interleaved Proposition 5.2), by computing the inner product of an induced character with itself from an explicit induced character table built on a primitive root of unity, by counting the two families of parameters s for which (q^2-1) divides s(q +- 1) against those where it does not, and then by summing the resulting degrees to obtain the total character degree q^4 + q^3 + q of G and comparing it with the largest irreducible degree q^4 + 2q^3 + 2q^2 + 2q + 1 of Sp_4(q). Every step is carried out in the article rather than quoted from a textbook, and the argument is one of the cases of the article's main classification, which places the unit above ordinary PhD qualifying examinations in finite group representation theory.
